newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN BET ON BASLER TO COME UP TRUMPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN BET ON BASLER TO COME UP TRUMPS.

text.p: Bayern Munich's Mario Basler is a risk-taker on the soccer pitch but his off-field gambling has attracted almost as much attention over the last few months.

The brilliant midfielder, a key player in Sunday's derby match with 1860 Munich, is enjoying a wave of good form which culminated in a glorious goal for the German national side in Wednesday's 2-0 win over Ukraine.

But Basler, who joined Bayern from Werder Bremen last year, still has to persuade sceptics that he is a true professional when it comes to preparing for the big games and making the most of his undisputed talents.
The 28-year-old Basler came under heavy fire when it emerged that he had been playing cards into the early hours on the day of Bayern's clash with Bayer Leverkusen in March.
The incident would scarcely have merited a mention normally -- but a shambolic Bayern lost the match 5-2.
"I know it was a mistake," Basler admits. "But you can't change things now."
His reputation was hardly enhanced the following month when he was spotted enjoying a night in a Bavarian casino while Germany were struggling to a 3-2 win over Albania in Spain.

Berti Vogts had allowed Basler to withdraw from the squad for the Albania match to be in Germany for the birth of his son. But Basler insists Vogts was not annoyed when he heard that one of his star midfielders had been out gambling instead.
"The coach told me I could do what I liked in my free time," he said. "Who knows what other players who weren't with the squad were doing?"

Basler's penchant for the good life -- he also smokes a packet of cigarettes a day, enjoys Germany's famous beers and takes a keen interest in horse racing --- appears to have had little effect on his form over the last few weeks.
Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni has moved Basler into central midfield to cover for Mehmet Scholl, who has been absent due to injury and a crisis in confidence.
Basler has flourished in his new role, scoring freely, linking well with strikers Juergen Klinsmann and Ruggiero Rizzitelli and firing in dangerous free kicks and corners.

With Scholl apparently out of the reckoning at the moment, Trapattoni has little option other than to put all his chips on Basler to provide the genius to overcome 1860 and guide them to their first Bundesliga title since 1994.
